quarterly_data.quarter: Astera Labs Citi’s Global TMT Conference 2026 (09-09-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: SCORPIO X ENGAGEMENTS RAISED FROM 10 TO HIGH TEENS, FIVE WEEKS AFTER THE Q2 CALL: CFO Desmond Lynch said that what Astera had talked about initially was 'having 10 customer engagements' for Scorpio X, and 'that number now today is up into the high teens, and we expect to convert several of these opportunities into design wins by the end of the year', with revenue from those following in 2027. He added that across the whole portfolio Astera is now 'shipping to all of the U.S.-based hyperscalers', with Scorpio P diversification coming from additional hyperscaler customers and AI infrastructure providers beyond the lead customer, while the lead customer continues to grow. CEO Jitendra Mohan said the 320-lane Scorpio X introduced in Q2 is 'already entering volume production here in Q3', is already shipping to the lead customer and is shipping to additional customers, with many actively designing it in to ramp in 2027 - a multi-quarter deployment with multiple applications inside the lead customer.
quarterly_data.figure: 10 customer engagements; up into the high teens; design wins by the end of the year

quarterly_data.quarter: Astera Labs Citi’s Global TMT Conference 2026 (09-09-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: SCORPIO P SIZED AND THE COMPETITIVE FRAME AGAINST BROADCOM: Mohan disclosed that Scorpio P, introduced at OCP in October of 2024 for scale-out connectivity (GPUs to NICs and CPUs), became the fastest-growing product line and that 'just in three quarters last year, it was 15% of our total revenue'. Astera has since 'added another hyperscaler customer' and is into multiple customers deploying Scorpio P. On competition he said that before Astera entered, 'the dominant switch supplier was actually Broadcom with their PCIe Gen 5 switch products', while Astera is now 'shipping this in the highest volume for PCI Express Gen 6'; he expects competition to arrive in both P and X given the TAM and said it is not a zero-sum game.
quarterly_data.figure: 15% of our total revenue; highest volume for PCI Express Gen 6

quarterly_data.quarter: Astera Labs Citi’s Global TMT Conference 2026 (09-09-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: CONTENT PER XPU: FROM SUB $100 AT IPO TO CLOSE TO $1,000 TODAY, WITH SCORPIO X ALONE TARGETED AT $1,000+: Mohan walked the content ladder - at IPO content per XPU was 'sub $100, largely driven by the Aries retimer products that were attached to the Hopper GPU', and 'now we are already at close to $1,000 of content' across Aries, Taurus, Leo CXL and Scorpio. Astera is 'on track to get $1,000 or more content on a per XPU basis from the Scorpio X family alone', with new product families (optical in particular) taking content into 'multiple thousands of dollars' per XPU. He also framed the demand backdrop with hyperscaler CapEx 'now expected to cross $1 trillion next year' and the unit of compute having moved from eight Hopper GPUs on an HGX board at IPO to a full rack today, as models crossed 10 trillion parameters.
quarterly_data.figure: sub $100; close to $1,000 of content; $1,000 or more content on a per XPU basis from the Scorpio X family alone

quarterly_data.quarter: Astera Labs Citi’s Global TMT Conference 2026 (09-09-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: OPTICAL TIMELINE TIGHTENED - CONNECTOR REVENUE 2027, NPO REVENUE IN 2H 2027, CPO AT 400G PER LANE: Mohan said optical revenue starts in 2027 with component-level sales of the glass coupler/connector from the aiXscale Photonics acquisition closed 'in December of last year', which customers are qualifying for their own CPU scale-out applications and which 'might very well end up becoming the first revenue that we see in 2027'. Next is NPO, which Astera considers the right answer at '200 gig per lane data rates' because it does not stress the supply chain while delivering the distance and density scale-up needs; 'we will start to see initial revenues in the back half of 2027 from our NPO efforts. Then full year ahead in 2028.' At '400 gig per lane data rates and even higher densities' CPO takes over, with Astera supplying the full optical engine - its own electrical IC, its own photonics IC (PIC) and the fiber-to-silicon-photonics packaging - landing both on an optically enabled Scorpio SKU and on the XPU side, so a link that previously had no such component gains two. He also corrected a pricing assumption for multi-rack scale-up: as cluster sizes go from 72 to 144, 288 and 576 GPUs the switch radix rises and 'contrary to popular belief that price per lane goes down, it actually goes up with radix'.
quarterly_data.figure: initial revenues in the back half of 2027; 200 gig per lane; 400 gig per lane

quarterly_data.quarter: Astera Labs Citi’s Global TMT Conference 2026 (09-09-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: NVLINK FUSION ECONOMICS QUANTIFIED AS A WASH WHERE IT SUBSTITUTES, INCREMENTAL WHERE IT DOES NOT: Mohan said NVLink Fusion lets Astera help customers attach their own XPUs to NVIDIA's NVL72 or MGX platforms. Where a customer has both paths - he cited AWS, which has publicly said it will have a native solution with a UALink switch as well as an NVLink Fusion solution - 'the total revenue opportunity on a per rack basis is about the same given the differences in attach rate and ASP. Maybe it is a wash.' Where customers instead want to use NVIDIA infrastructure to deploy their XPU, 'that becomes net positive incremental TAM that is available to us', and he read NVIDIA's willingness to let Astera deploy NVLink infrastructure with other customers as a trust signal. Astera's stated goal is to address the full scale-up TAM across NVLink, PCI Express, UALink and Ethernet.
quarterly_data.figure: total revenue opportunity on a per rack basis is about the same

quarterly_data.quarter: Astera Labs Citi’s Global TMT Conference 2026 (09-09-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: WHY MI450 RUNS UALINK OVER ETHERNET, AND WHAT IT MEANS FOR ASTERA CONTENT: asked about the first Helios server, CEO Jitendra Mohan declined to speak for AMD but reiterated AMD's public position - 'for the MI450 series, they are going to go with UALink running over Ethernet. That has really got everything to do with the fact that UALink switches are not yet available', so MI450 must tunnel UALink over Ethernet - while AMD has said it will keep offering both UALink over Ethernet and native UALink in future generations, which Mohan expects to coexist. The content consequence he spelled out generically: where Astera does not supply the scale-up switching, its content is limited to scale-out retimers, Scorpio P, Taurus Ethernet retimers and active electrical cables; where the scale-up protocol is one Astera supports (PCI Express, UALink or something in between) and a Scorpio X solution can be used, 'then our content really does explode a lot, because scale up is a very rich area for connectivity solutions'. He added that the in-network compute, Hypercast, diagnostics and telemetry built into today's Scorpio X, exposed through COSMOS software, carry forward to a UALink-based Scorpio X, making the migration easy for existing Scorpio X users.
